name: Golden Mountains of Altai
blurb: Steppe to alpine slopes where snow leopards hunt ibex and argali.

tip.title: Remove the Siberian ibex
tip.text: Set Siberian ibex to -100% and watch the snow leopard and wolf lose a main prey, and cinereous vultures lose carrion.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer light drives growth on the alpine meadows and steppe slopes; the growing season is short at altitude.

nodes.name: Snowmelt and glacier water
nodes.desc: Meltwater from winter snow and the glaciers around Belukha feeds the meadows and the rivers below.

nodes.name: Cold, snowy winters
nodes.desc: Deep cold and snow shape which plants survive and push animals such as ibex to lower slopes in winter.

nodes.name: Mountain soils
nodes.desc: Thin mountain and steppe soils hold the nutrients that plants draw on and that decomposers return.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Siberian larch
nodes.desc: A deciduous conifer that is among the most recorded plants near the site and forms much of the forest belt on the slopes.

nodes.name: Siberian pine
nodes.desc: A five-needled pine of the mountain taiga whose large seeds are a food for birds such as the nutcracker.

nodes.name: Steppe and alpine grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses and sedges of the steppe and alpine meadows, the main food of the wild sheep, goats and small grazers.

nodes.name: Shrubby cinquefoil
nodes.desc: A low shrub of mountain meadows and rocky ground; GloBI records bears and other animals feeding on it.

nodes.name: Siberian ibex
nodes.desc: A wild goat of steep rocky slopes that eats grasses and herbs, and twigs and needles in winter. Snow leopards and wolves prey on it.

nodes.name: Argali
nodes.desc: The largest wild sheep, grazing grasses, sedges and herbs on open slopes. Wolves and snow leopards prey on it, and golden eagles take lambs.

nodes.name: Gray marmot
nodes.desc: A burrowing rodent of mountain meadows and steppe that eats grasses and flowering plants. Many predators take it, including wolves, foxes and birds of prey.

nodes.name: Long-tailed ground squirrel
nodes.desc: A burrowing ground squirrel of steppe and meadows and the most recorded mammal near the site. Steppe eagles and foxes take it.

nodes.name: Alpine pika
nodes.desc: A small lagomorph living among scree and rocks that eats meadow plants. Snow leopards also hunt small mammals such as pikas.

nodes.name: Narrow-headed vole
nodes.desc: A small grass-eating vole of steppe and meadow; foxes, stoats, eagles and bears are recorded eating it in GloBI.

nodes.name: Eurasian nutcracker
nodes.desc: A crow-family bird that feeds on conifer seeds, especially pine seeds, and stores them in caches.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A flexible predator recorded in GloBI eating many species here, from voles and marmots to birds, lizards and berries.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: A small weasel that hunts voles and other small prey, including birds and lizards, in meadows and scree.

nodes.name: Steppe eagle
nodes.desc: A large eagle of open country that hunts ground squirrels, marmots, voles and hares.

nodes.name: Cinereous vulture
nodes.desc: A huge vulture that feeds mostly on carrion, such as dead wild and domestic hoofed animals, and also takes marmots.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore of the forests and meadows that eats plants and berries as well as marmots, voles and other animals.

nodes.name: Snow leopard
nodes.desc: The high-mountain cat of the Altai, living on rocky broken ground. Its main prey here includes Siberian ibex and argali, plus marmots and pikas.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: A pack hunter that preys on wild sheep and goats such as argali and ibex, and also takes marmots.
